title: ReSCUE: Re-translation with Sentence Commitment for Unsegmented Long-Form Simultaneous Sign Language Translation
claim: A streaming system chunks continuous input, re-translates a buffer with consistency, and commits finished sentences to history to bound memory and latency.
layout: Top video strip, three-column pipeline left-to-right, buffer timeline on left, legend top-right
description: The top strip shows a sign-language video split into labeled chunks x_{t-2} to x_{t+1}, with a ground-truth caption overlaid and a legend at top right. Below, a green Input Buffer panel on the left lists time steps t-1, t and t+1 as stacked rows of green in-buffer and white out-of-buffer chunk tiles. A black arrow at the far left points down along the time axis. The center panel, Stabilized Re-Translation, shows a pipeline of pose estimator, pose encoder and multimodal LLM, with pose skeleton images between them. On the right, blue speech bubbles show the previous hypothesis and the current hypothesis, linked by a dotted prefix-consistency arrow. A grey Committed History box feeds the concatenated user-facing output. A bottom Sentence Commitment bar checks for silence or terminal punctuation, and red dashed arrows update the buffer start and the history.
caption: Overview of the proposed simultaneous SLT pipeline. The unsegmented video stream is processed in fixed-length chunks and accumulated in a dynamic input buffer. At each step, the SLT module performs re-translation over the buffered video segment to produce a revisable hypothesis for the current sentence, while encouraging prefix consistency with the previous hypothesis. Finalized translations of previous sentences are stored in the committed history and concatenated with the current hypothesis to form the user-facing output. A sentence commitment mechanism detects sentence completion, extracts the finalized translation, appends it to the committed history, and advances the input buffer accordingly.
abstract: Simultaneous Sign Language Translation (SLT) is critical for real-time communication, yet existing methods remain largely confined to sentence-level, offline settings that assume pre-segmented inputs. These assumptions hinder deployment in realistic scenarios involving continuous, unsegmented video streams. We present ReSCUE, a unified framework for simultaneous SLT on unsegmented long-form sign language videos that aligns training and inference with realistic streaming conditions. ReSCUE combines inference-aware training to handle partial inputs, non-signing pauses, and multi-sentence contexts, stabilized re-translation to enable low-latency yet revisable predictions with reduced output flicker, and a sentence commitment mechanism for online segmentation and memory management. Experiments on standard sentence-level benchmarks show that ReSCUE achieves lower latency and the best translation quality under low-latency settings. On long-form unsegmented datasets, ReSCUE approaches the translation quality of oracle offline systems that use ground-truth sentence boundaries, while operating at substantially lower latency, demonstrating its practicality for real-world streaming scenarios.
